h17.title: Durable Medical Equipment: Protecting Medicare and Medicaid from Fraud, Waste, and Abuse
h17.snippet: OIG feature noting Medicare DMEPOS payments exceed $7 billion annually and fraudulent billing schemes continue to evolve, including equipment billed but never received.

h17.title: OIG to CMS: Stronger fraud efforts are needed for DMEPOS
h17.snippet: Prior OIG analysis found evidence of automatic shipping of PAP/CPAP supplies with no physician orders for refills in effect; automatic resupply shipment is not permitted under Medicare rules.

h17.title: Consumer Alert: Urinary Catheter Scams
h17.snippet: OIG consumer alert describing recurring-supply fraud pattern: monthly billing for medically unnecessary catheters that may or may not actually be shipped to the beneficiary.

h21.title: Telehealth Sector Wake-Up Call: CEO Sentenced to 15 Years, Ordered to Pay $452M for $1B Medicare Fraud Scheme (DMERx)
h21.snippet: DMERx platform generated false doctors' orders for orthotic braces; telemedicine physicians paid kickbacks to sign orders without examining patients; DME suppliers billed over $1 billion using the resulting orders.

h21.title: Physician Convicted In $6.3 Million Medicare Fraud Scheme: Lessons For DME Suppliers
h21.snippet: New Jersey telemedicine-company owner paid kickbacks to providers to sign orthotic brace orders for beneficiaries with no clinical need; signed orders resold through marketing companies to brace suppliers, generating over $56 million in claims.

h21.title: Fraudulent Telehealth Arrangements In The DME Space
h21.snippet: Overview of recurring telehealth-to-DME referral fraud pattern: overseas call centers collect beneficiary information, telehealth physicians sign orders without a treating relationship, DME suppliers bill Medicare on the resulting orders.

h28.title: Telehealth Sector Wake-Up Call: CEO Sentenced to 15 Years, Ordered to Pay $452M for $1B Medicare Fraud Scheme (DMERx)
h28.snippet: Scheme concealed telemedicine origin of orders by removing words like "telemedicine" or "phone conversation" from doctors' orders to avoid triggering DME supplier audits tied to ordering-provider concentration.

h28.title: Physician Convicted In $6.3 Million Medicare Fraud Scheme: Lessons For DME Suppliers
h28.snippet: Kansas anesthesiologist signed fraudulent DME prescriptions without examining patients or establishing a treating relationship, falsely certifying medical necessity; Medicare paid at least $8 million on his orders alone — illustrating single-prescriber concentration risk.

h04.title: A Review of Claims for Capped Rental Durable Medical Equipment (OEI-07-08-00550)
h04.snippet: OIG review found Medicare erroneously allowed nearly $4.4 million (2006-2008) for repairs of capped-rental DME, since repair costs are already included in the monthly rental payment and are not separately payable; 48% of claims lacked sufficient information to identify make/model.

h04.title: Capped Rental Items - JD DME
h04.snippet: MAC reference describing capped-rental fee schedule mechanics (10% first month, 7.5% months 2-15, no further payment after 15 months except maintenance/servicing) and modifier usage for oxygen equipment.

h06.title: A Review of Claims for Capped Rental Durable Medical Equipment (OEI-07-08-00550)
h06.snippet: OIG found suppliers did not provide serial numbers for 25% of repair claims and provided invalid serial numbers for 23% more, preventing verification of which physical unit was being billed — a documentation gap directly relevant to detecting supplier-switch anniversary-date resets.

h06.title: OIG Review Finds Erroneous Capped Rental DME Claims
h06.snippet: Of $90 million allowed for capped-rental DME repair claims in 2007, nearly $27 million was associated with payment errors, underscoring weak controls around the capped-rental episode lifecycle.

h22.title: A Review of Claims for Capped Rental Durable Medical Equipment (OEI-07-08-00550)
h22.snippet: Same OIG review documents systemic inability to verify equipment identity/continuity across capped-rental claims, the core weakness a rotating-supplier network would exploit to fragment a beneficiary's rental history across multiple NPIs.

h22.title: 12031-P DMEPOS Temporary Gap Period fact sheet
h22.snippet: CMS fact sheet on temporary gap-period rules affecting rental continuity determinations, relevant to how a coordinated supplier network could time claims around gap-period boundaries.

h11.title: A Review of Claims for Capped Rental Durable Medical Equipment (OEI-07-08-00550)
h11.snippet: OIG documentation-gap findings on capped-rental claims support the difficulty payers have verifying whether a claimed 60+ day medical-need interruption was genuine versus manufactured to reset the 15-month capped-rental clock.

h19.title: Part B Services During Non-Part A Nursing Home Stays
h19.snippet: OIG review of Part B billing during non-Part A nursing home stays, directly relevant to boundary-switching risk between institutional and home settings for DME billing.

h19.title: Inappropriate and Questionable Billing by Medicare Home Health Agencies
h19.snippet: OIG review identifying questionable billing patterns by home health agencies, providing precedent for scrutinizing the HHA/DME consolidated-billing boundary.

h16.title: A Review of Claims for Capped Rental Durable Medical Equipment (OEI-07-08-00550)
h16.snippet: Same capped-rental/oxygen documentation-gap findings apply directly to volume-modifier and ownership-state cycling on oxygen equipment claims.

h16.title: Capped Rental Items - JD DME
h16.snippet: MAC guidance on oxygen contents-fee and volume-modifier (QG/QF/QB) mechanics underlying this hypothesis.

h05.title: Custom Fitted Orthotic HCPCS Codes Without a Corresponding Off-the-Shelf Code - Correct Coding
h05.snippet: MAC correct-coding guidance confirming that billing a custom-fabricated code for a prefabricated/off-the-shelf item constitutes upcoding, and that miscellaneous codes (L1499/L2999/L3999) must be used when no specific code exists — directly relevant to E1399 misuse.

h05.title: HCPCS Code L3000: Custom Foot Orthotic Billing
h05.snippet: Billing guide noting that billing L3000 for a prefabricated insert constitutes fraud; a custom item must be fabricated from a patient-specific cast, foam mold, or digital scan. Orthotic upcoding is a standing OIG audit priority.
